_about: Fire de-escalation planner rule table (Pavilion Cerebro, key 'fire'). Every threshold carries a public URL or the tag 'team-proposed, validate'. Kept inside cascade.building (not in cascade/rubrics) so drift fingerprints are unaffected. Sources accessed 2026-09-26 by the research and verify agents; corrections from the verifier applied.

thresholds.meaning: voice alarm reaches at least the floor above the alarming floor
thresholds.note: IBC 2021 907.5.2.2: 'at least the alarming floor, the floor above and the floor below'; LAFD high-rise sequence policy footnote a says the same for new high-rises

thresholds.meaning: voice alarm reaches at least the floor below the alarming floor
fire department staging at least this many floors below the fire floor
thresholds.note: Sacramento Regional Fire guideline (reviewed 08/21/22): 'Staging a minimum of two floors below'. California regional guideline, not an LAFD SOP

thresholds.meaning: hose line connects to the standpipe in the attack stair this many floors below the fire
thresholds.note: Sacramento guideline: 'Equipment should be placed outside fire attack stairwell one floor below'; IBC 905.4 puts a hose connection at every floor landing

thresholds.meaning: crews leave the fire service elevator at least this many floors below the fire
thresholds.note: Sacramento guideline: 'crews exit a minimum of two floors below'; Phase II is fire department only

thresholds.meaning: fire department elevator use expected only when the fire floor is at or above this level
thresholds.note: Sacramento guideline: 'Elevator use is authorized for fires above the sixth floor'; below that the card says stairs expected

thresholds.meaning: highest relocation floor is at least this many floors below the fire floor (below the staging floor)
thresholds.note: NIST TN 1664 reports an 'evacuate down three floors' message in a real high-rise fire; not a code rule. The building's approved Emergency Plan overrides this

thresholds.meaning: number of relocation floors offered to occupants of the alert floors
thresholds.note: sized so the design load of three alert floors fits; validate with the Emergency Plan relocation areas

thresholds.meaning: floors above the alert zone whose shaft and core readings are watched for smoke spread
thresholds.note: NISTIR 89-4035: stairwells and elevator shafts frequently become smoke-logged (stack effect). The band width is our choice

thresholds.meaning: an alarm this many floors or more above the fire floor is treated as possible upward spread (escalation trigger E2)
thresholds.note: First Interstate 1988 spread upward from floor 12 to floor 16

thresholds.meaning: IBC business occupant load factor used for the design occupant load (a code design figure, not a headcount)
thresholds.note: Jensen Hughes memo, 2023-12-01: IBC 2018+ business load factor changed from 100 to 150 sq ft per person

thresholds.meaning: high-rise exit stair enclosures at least 30 ft apart (or 1/4 of the diagonal), measured between the nearest points of the enclosures
thresholds.note: IBC 403.5.1 summary; scissor stairs count as one stairway. The synthetic layout is checked against this but no IBC compliance is claimed

thresholds.meaning: stair pressurization range (0.10-0.35 in. water) that the listed smoke-control system maintains
stair cameras on every 5th floor landing, viewable from the fire control room
thresholds.note: LAFD Requirement No. 10, Option 2 EHLF Equivalency only. Not a general high-rise requirement

thresholds.meaning: IBC 403 height triggers (highest occupied floor above fire department access)
an energy storage (battery) room within this many floors of the fire is flagged 'near'
thresholds.note: UL FSRI Surprise AZ 2019 report recommends remote gas monitoring; the distance is our choice

thresholds.meaning: hop limit on the water graph when predicting where firefighting water migrates
thresholds.note: path score cut uses the existing REACH_MIN threshold of cascade.building.rules

automatic_sequence.item: Voice alarm on the alarm floor, the floor above and the floor below

automatic_sequence.condition: ONLY IF an elevator lobby or hoistway detector activates (LAFD matrix row 'Recall All Elevators', footnote g); manual pull, area smoke, duct detector and waterflow do not recall elevators

automatic_sequence.item: Smoke control and stair pressurization start
automatic_sequence.condition: per the building's approved smoke-control matrix

automatic_sequence.item: Air handlers shut down and dampers close
Held doors release and stair doors unlock
Annunciation at the fire control room and the 24-hour remote station

decisions.question: AI early alert with no listed alarm: check by camera; if staff must look, they go by stair, never by elevator. Fire seen: pull the alarm and call 911.
Call 911 (or designate someone). The AI never delays or replaces this call.
Approve the protect strategy (alert and relocation floors, evacuation stair) and read one consistent voice message live.
Fire department incident commander takes command; building systems move only on IC orders; IC designates the attack and evacuation stairs.
Widen the alert zone or order a total evacuation when an escalation trigger fires.
Authorize resets, fire watch where systems are impaired, and re-occupancy.

triggers.text: An alarm or waterflow signal on a floor outside the alert set: add that floor and the floors next to it.
An alarm on the fire floor +2 or higher: possible upward spread [team-proposed, validate].
Smoke reported in the evacuation stair: FSD and IC choose another stair.
An open system impairment on any alert or relocation floor.
An alarm in the battery (ESS) room: nobody opens the door; remote gas readings only.
A person who needs help on an alert floor is not accounted for.

phases.name: Prepare
phases.ai: plan card per floor and zone, impairment list, drill tracking
phases.built: plan card per floor and zone and impairment list: built on the SYNTHETIC tower; drill tracking: not built
phases.human: FSD keeps the plan; LAFD approves the Emergency Plan

phases.name: Verify
phases.trigger: listed alarm, or an AI early alert (not an alarm)
phases.ai: camera frames and sensor-based fire/nuisance label near the device
phases.built: camera: not built (Part C out of scope); sensor label: built and tested, but it did not transfer to a new room (see results)

phases.name: Protect
phases.ai: draft plan card and one message template
phases.built: plan card: built; message template: not built
phases.human: D2: FSD approves and reads the message live

phases.name: Hand over
phases.ai: one-page briefing (stairs, standpipe landing, elevators, panels, risers, hazards)
phases.built: built: the plan card download (Markdown or JSON)

phases.name: Contain
phases.ai: read-only awareness: alarm spread, shaft readings, water below
phases.built: alarm spread (trigger E1/E2) and water below (SIMULATED water graph): built in the planner; live shaft readings: not built (the card lists which sensors to read)
phases.human: D4: IC widens the zone or evacuates fully

phases.name: Recover
phases.ai: reset checklist, salvage list for floors below
phases.built: salvage list (water watch): built; reset checklist: not built
phases.human: D5: IC authorizes resets and re-occupancy

phases.name: Learn
phases.built: automatic timeline: not built; plan card updates: rerun scripts/fire_build_plans.py

ai_never: silence, reset or delay any alarm, or delay the 911 call
command or override the firefighter's smoke control panel, sprinklers, fire pumps, elevator recall or Phase II, stair locks or HVAC
choose the evacuation scope (the FSD, then the fire department incident commander, decides)
send anyone toward the fire or up in an elevator to check an alarm
treat a 'nuisance-like' score as a reason to downgrade a code alarm

first_interstate.text: The fire started on floor 12 of the 62-story First Interstate Bank tower in Los Angeles (May 1988) and burned floors 12 to 16, spreading upward.
first_interstate.design_rule: plan for upward spread: the card watches floors above the alert zone and fires trigger E2

first_interstate.text: The sprinkler system was about 90 percent installed but not in service, and the standpipe had been shut off (drained down to floor 58 per the LAFD archive summary).
first_interstate.design_rule: show open system impairments at the top of the card (trigger E4)

first_interstate.text: A maintenance worker took a service elevator to floor 12 to check the alarm and died.
first_interstate.design_rule: check alarms remotely (cameras, sensors); if staff must go, by stair, never by elevator (decision D0)

first_interstate.text: About 50 people were above the fire; five were rescued from the roof by helicopter.
first_interstate.design_rule: list the roof landing and people needing help on the card
